title: Judges 9
paragraphs: ¹ Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem, to his mother's brothers, and spoke with them and with all his mother's family, saying, ² "Ask all the citizens of Shechem: which is better for you — that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or that one man rule over you? Remember that I am your own flesh and blood." ³ His mother's brothers repeated all these words to the citizens of Shechem, and their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother." ⁴ They gave him seventy pieces of silver from the temple of Baal-Berith, and with this money Abimelech hired worthless and reckless men, who followed him. ⁵ He went to his father's house at Ophrah and killed his brothers, the seventy sons of Jerubbaal, on a single stone. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, escaped by hiding.

⁶ Then all the citizens of Shechem and all Beth-millo gathered together and made Abimelech king, by the oak of the pillar at Shechem. ⁷ When Jotham heard this, he went and stood on top of Mount Gerizim and called out loudly: "Listen to me, citizens of Shechem, so that God may listen to you. ⁸ Once the trees went out to anoint a king over themselves. They said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.' ⁹ But the olive tree answered, 'Should I give up my rich oil, by which both gods and humans are honored, and go to hold sway over the trees?' ¹⁰ Next the trees said to the fig tree, 'Come and reign over us.'

¹¹ But the fig tree answered, 'Should I give up my sweetness and my good fruit, and go to hold sway over the trees?' ¹² Then the trees said to the vine, 'Come and reign over us.' ¹³ But the vine answered, 'Should I give up my wine, which cheers both gods and humans, and go to hold sway over the trees?' ¹⁴ Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, 'Come and reign over us.' ¹⁵ The thornbush said to the trees, 'If you really want to anoint me king over you, come and take shelter in my shade. But if not, let fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.'

¹⁶ Now then, if you have acted honorably and in good faith when you made Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his family and treated him as he deserved — ¹⁷ for my father fought for you and risked his life to rescue you from the hand of Midian, ¹⁸ but today you have risen against my father's house and killed his seventy sons on a single stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his slave girl, king over the citizens of Shechem, just because he is your relative — ¹⁹ if you have acted honorably and in good faith toward Jerubbaal and his family today, then may you be glad about Abimelech and may he be glad about you. ²⁰ But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and consume the citizens of Shechem and Beth-millo; and let fire come out from the citizens of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech."

²¹ Then Jotham fled, escaping to Beer, and lived there because he was afraid of his brother Abimelech. ²² After Abimelech had ruled over Israel for three years, ²³ God stirred up ill will between Abimelech and the citizens of Shechem, and the citizens of Shechem acted treacherously against Abimelech. ²⁴ This was so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might be avenged, and their blood might be charged against their brother Abimelech, who killed them, and against the citizens of Shechem, who gave him the strength to kill his brothers. ²⁵ In their hostility the citizens of Shechem set ambushers against him in the hills, and they robbed everyone who passed by. Abimelech was told about this.

²⁶ Now Gaal the son of Ebed came with his relatives and moved to Shechem, and the citizens of Shechem put their confidence in him. ²⁷ They went out into the fields, harvested their vineyards, trod the grapes, and held a festival. They went into the temple of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech. ²⁸ Gaal the son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who are we of Shechem, that we should serve him? Isn't he the son of Jerubbaal? And isn't Zebul his deputy? Serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem — why should we serve Abimelech? ²⁹ If only this people were under my command, then I would get rid of Abimelech." He said to Abimelech, "Muster your army and come out!" ³⁰ When Zebul the governor of the city heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger burned.

³¹ He sent messengers secretly to Abimelech, saying, "Gaal the son of Ebed and his relatives have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you. ³² So tonight you and your men should get up and lie in wait in the fields. ³³ In the morning at sunrise, advance against the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, do whatever you can to them." ³⁴ So Abimelech and all his men got up at night and positioned themselves in four groups near Shechem. ³⁵ Gaal the son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate. Abimelech and his troops rose from their hiding places.

³⁶ When Gaal saw the troops, he said to Zebul, "Look, there are people coming down from the mountaintops!" But Zebul replied, "You're seeing the shadows of the mountains — they look like people." ³⁷ Gaal spoke again: "Look, there are people coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming from the direction of the oak of Meonenim." ³⁸ Zebul said to him, "Where's all your boasting now — when you said, 'Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?' Aren't these the troops you despised? Go out now and fight them!" ³⁹ So Gaal led the citizens of Shechem out and fought against Abimelech. ⁴⁰ Abimelech chased him, and Gaal fled. Many fell wounded all the way to the entrance of the gate.

⁴¹ Abimelech returned to Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaal and his relatives so they could no longer live in Shechem. ⁴² The next day the people of Shechem went out into the fields, and Abimelech was told about it. ⁴³ He took his men, divided them into three companies, and set an ambush in the fields. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose and attacked them. ⁴⁴ Abimelech and his company rushed forward and took up a position at the entrance of the city gate, while the other two companies charged all the people who were in the fields and struck them down. ⁴⁵ Abimelech fought against the city all that day. He captured it, killed its people, demolished the city, and sowed it with salt.

⁴⁶ When all the people of the Tower of Shechem heard this, they went into the stronghold of the temple of El-Berith. ⁴⁷ Abimelech was told that all the people of the Tower of Shechem had gathered there. ⁴⁸ He and all his troops went up to Mount Zalmon. Abimelech took an ax in his hand, cut off a bundle of branches, lifted it onto his shoulder, and said to his men, "Hurry — do what you see me doing!" ⁴⁹ So each of his men also cut a bundle and followed Abimelech. They piled the branches against the stronghold and set it on fire over those inside. All the people of the Tower of Shechem also died — about a thousand men and women. ⁵⁰ Then Abimelech went to Thebez and besieged it and captured it.

⁵¹ But inside the city was a strong tower, and all the men and women — everyone in the city — fled into it. They locked themselves in and climbed up to the roof. ⁵² Abimelech came up to the tower door to set it on fire. ⁵³ But a woman dropped an upper millstone on his head and cracked his skull. ⁵⁴ He quickly called to his armor-bearer and said, "Draw your sword and run me through, so no one can say a woman killed me." His young man ran him through, and he died. ⁵⁵ When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went back to their homes.

⁵⁶ In this way God repaid the wickedness that Abimelech had done to his father by killing his seventy brothers. ⁵⁷ And God also repaid the men of Shechem for all their wickedness. The curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal came true against them.
